narratives.Overview:
## Scan provenance

AppSec scan of `deftai/directive` @ `764f63a6` (2026-08-31, Cursor Grok 4.5, scan-only, no PR opened). PoCs re-verified on that commit. Stored in scanner memory as -25 / -26.

Filed set after the scanner's own retraction: **3 HIGH + 1 MEDIUM**. The three MEDIUM leaf-diversion items originally reported (`vbrief-validation/safety.ts`, `vbrief-reconcile/reconciliation.ts`, `vbrief-build/speckit.ts`) were retracted by the scanner and are **not** part of this issue: `migrate:vbrief` is unshipped on current npm and those sinks have no production CLI caller (test/parity only), matching the earlier dismissal in memory -11.

## HIGH 1 - Grok `run_terminal_command` bypasses the UAT Shell authz classifier

**Location:** `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts` (`classifyHookAuthzOps`)

`classifyHookAuthzOps` carries its own tool-name gate instead of using the shared helper:

```ts
const lower = toolName.toLowerCase();
if (lower.includes("bash") || lower.includes("shell") || lower === "run_terminal_cmd") {
  if (shellCommand === null) return [];
  return classifyShellAuthzOps(shellCommand);
}
```

`packages/core/src/hooks/tools.ts` already lists `run_terminal_command` in `SHELL_TOOL_NAMES`, so `isShellTool("run_terminal_command")` is `true` and `hooks/dispatcher.ts` extracts the command string for it. The private gate above accepts only `run_terminal_cmd` (the Cursor spelling), so on Grok Build the whole classified Shell corpus falls through to the unrelated-tool `return []` -- allow / shell-op-unclassifiable.

**Impact:** `cp` / `echo >` / `tee` / `printf` / `dd` / `install` / `touch` into `.deft/authz/**`, `.deft-directive-disable`, or `.deft/approved-scope/**` is allowed on Grok while the identical `Bash` / `Shell` command is denied with `authz-grant-missing` under UAT. Two layers disagree on the same host tool: the dispatcher treats it as a shell tool, the authz classifier does not.

**Remediation:** route the authz name gate through `isShellTool(toolName)` (or at minimum add `run_terminal_command`), and add a test that keeps the classifier's host-name coverage tied to `SHELL_TOOL_NAMES` so a new host spelling cannot land in one layer only.

**Regression test:** `Bash` `cp <src> .deft/authz/<file>` and Grok `run_terminal_command` with the same command both classify as `settings` and deny under UAT.

Related but distinct: **#3987** covers deposited-matcher / `hooks/tools.ts` coverage for this host's tool spellings; the `tools.ts` half is present, the authz classifier's duplicated gate is not.

## HIGH 2 - UAT residual Shell writers plant `.deft/authz` grants

**Location:** `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts`

Residual writers not classified by the shell classifier (none of these strings appear in `classify.ts`):

`nu`, `xonsh`, `truffleruby`, `mruby`, `opal`, `rbx`, `ipython3`, `bpython`, `ptpython`, `ghc`, `ocaml`, `zip`, `haxe`, `kak`, `helix`, `amp`, `redis-cli`, `ctr`, `rst2html`, `tclsh`, `expect`, `xdelta3`, `diffoscope`, `parcel`, `serverless`, `dar`, `borg`, `duplicity`, `curlftpfs`, `rpmbuild`

**Impact:** `classify` returns `[]` -> allow -> forged operator-cli grant in `.deft/authz` -> subsequent edit / push / PR / merge proceed as authorized.

**Remediation:** classify these writers when the destination touches `.deft/authz`, and fail closed on unclassifiable write-shaped Shell under UAT rather than allowing.

Same family as #3626 / #3728 / #3764 / #3804 / #3849 / #3918 / #3953 (post-#3545 residuals).

## HIGH 3 - Same residual writers plant `.deft-directive-disable`

**Location:** `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts`

**Impact:** planting the kill-switch file yields the #3039 all-tool Directive bypass for the remainder of the session.

**Remediation:** same classify coverage plus fail-closed posture for the kill-switch basenames.

## MEDIUM - Same residual writers forge `.deft/approved-scope`

**Location:** `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts`

**Impact:** bypasses the human-presence mint gate for provenance-approval artifacts.

**Remediation:** extend the approved-scope classify path to the same residual writer family.

## Acceptance

- Grok `run_terminal_command` and `Bash` produce identical authz classifications for the same command string, asserted by test.
- The authz classifier's shell-host name set is derived from (or verified against) `SHELL_TOOL_NAMES`, so host spellings cannot drift between the dispatcher and the classifier.
- Each residual writer above, when its destination touches `.deft/authz/**`, `.deft-directive-disable`, or `.deft/approved-scope/**`, classifies as a gated op; write-shaped Shell that cannot be classified fails closed under UAT.

Refs #3545, #2711, #3039, #3186, #3987

### Comment by @dbcall2 (2026-09-02T20:16:54Z)

model: claude-opus-5[1m]
role: critic

**Verdict: the recorded premise does not survive.** All three of its limbs fail against the tree at the dispatch SHA and against executed probes of the classifier. The exposure behind HIGH 2 / HIGH 3 / MEDIUM is real and I reproduced it; the premise's remedy for it is a no-op on the corpus that motivates it, and limb 1 is already landed. HIGH 1 and HIGH 2/3/MEDIUM also do not share a root, so "as one issue" is a composition error on top of the mechanism errors.

Ceiling honored: issue body plus comments `5495382649`, `5495644104`, `5496118753`, `5515687443`. Everything else below is the tree at `212481b98051e9988f0a15748400c6afc154b2a5` and executed output, plus cross-issue upstream state read from #3997 / #3953 / #4041 / #3987.

## How I checked

Detached worktree at the dispatch SHA. Anchors re-read with `git show 212481b9:<path>`, and the classifier imported unmodified and executed with `tsx`:

```
git show 212481b9:packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts
git show 212481b9:packages/core/src/hooks/tools.ts
git show 212481b9:packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts
git show 212481b9:packages/core/src/authz/evaluate.ts
tsx probe.ts   # imports classifyShellAuthzOps / classifyHookAuthzOps from this worktree
```

Probes: 30 named residual writers x 3 protected dests x 5 command shapes, plus known-bin controls, plus host-name parity across `SHELL_TOOL_NAMES`.

## HIGH 1 is closed at the dispatch SHA — `blocks-the-design`

The gate the issue quotes no longer exists. `classifyHookAuthzOps` (`packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts:2858`) now reads `if (isShellTool(toolName))`, `SHELL_TOOL_NAMES` (`packages/core/src/hooks/tools.ts`) carries `run_terminal_command` and `monitor`, and `classify.test.ts` iterates that catalog asserting Bash parity on the three plant commands. Landed as `75d5970a` for #4041. Executed, same command string `cp /tmp/grant.json .deft/authz/grants/evil.json`:

```
Shell / Bash / BashTool / shell / bash / run_terminal_command / monitor  ->  ["settings"]
run_terminal_cmd                                                        ->  []   (isShellTool=false)
```

Acceptance item 2 is satisfied twice, not zero times: the #4041 parity test, and `packages/core/src/init-deposit/host-tool-coverage.ts`, which reads the deposited matchers and returns `uncovered-tool` / `unclassified-tool` when a catalogued host spelling is missing from a matcher or lands in a different classifier group. That is the "cannot land in one layer only" mechanism the issue asks to build.

**Failure mode of binding limb 1 anyway.** A builder handed this issue reads its own remediation text ("or at minimum add `run_terminal_command`") plus the quoted private gate's `run_terminal_cmd`, and adds the Cursor spelling to `SHELL_TOOL_NAMES`. That breaks two pinned assertions (`classify.test.ts` `expect(SHELL_TOOL_NAMES).not.toContain("run_terminal_cmd")`, `tools.test.ts` `isShellTool("run_terminal_cmd") === false`) and widens the shell matcher for a host whose emitted tool names `HOST_TOOL_SURFACE_AUDIT.cursor` explicitly records as unobserved. **Disposition consequence:** the target must be re-cut to exclude HIGH 1; there is nothing left to remediate there.

## Limb 3 ("fail closed on unclassifiable write-shaped Shell") is a no-op on this corpus — `blocks-the-design`

`hasWriteShape` (`classify.ts:2482`) is three things: `command.includes(">")`, membership in `INDIRECT_WRITE_BINS`, membership in `ARCHIVE_ALT_WRITE_BINS`. None of the 30 named writers is in either set, and the `>` arm is what already gates them. Executed, per shape, against `.deft/authz/grants/evil.json` over all 30 names:

| Shape | Gated |
|---|---|
| `W -c 'x' > <dest>` | 30/30 |
| `W -o <dest>` | 30/30 |
| `W --output <dest>` | 30/30 |
| `W <dest>` (positional) | 0/30 |
| `W -c "open('<dest>','w').write('x')"` | 0/30 |

So fail-closing on write shape adds enforcement exactly where enforcement already exists, and adds none where it does not. **Failure mode:** the remediation ships, its regression tests use redirect shapes (green before the change), the issue closes, and `nu -c "'x' | save .deft/authz/grants/evil.json"` still returns `[]` -> `shell-op-unclassifiable` -> allow -> forged operator-cli grant. **Disposition consequence:** limb 3 must be re-specified against destination visibility, not write shape, or dropped.

## Limb 2 enumerates on the axis that does not discriminate — `blocks-the-design`

In the three shapes that gate, they gate bin-independently — the dest is recovered and the bin name is never consulted. In the two shapes that do not gate, the bin lists are the whole discriminator: `tee <dest>` and `python3 <dest>` gate positionally, `python3 -c "open(<dest>,'w')…"` gates inline, while all 30 names are open in both. Adding 30 names therefore closes 60 cells and leaves both shape classes open for name 31, which the next scan supplies — the issue body itself lists seven prior sibling harvests, #3849 and #3953 are still open, and the accepted #3953 map (comment `5496071758`) already dominated #4005 HIGH 2/3/MEDIUM into a dest-based classifier story with named bins as regression corpus rather than implementation stories. I reached the same axis from execution before reading that map; the probe table above is the independent evidence for it. **Failure mode:** an AppSec scan one cycle later files the identical HIGH with 30 different names, against a classifier that just grew a 30-name list. **Disposition consequence:** HIGH 2/3/MEDIUM are corpus for that tracker, and this issue is not the remediation vehicle for them.

## The fail-closed mechanism already exists and has no producer — `sharpens-framing`

`AuthzClassifiedOp` includes `"unknown"` (`classify.ts:19`), and `evaluate.ts:323` denies it under an active UAT campaign with `authz-uat-deny` and operator recovery text. Grepped `packages/core/src`: nothing produces `"unknown"`. The deny arm the premise wants is written, tested at the evaluator, and unreachable. **Failure mode:** limb 3 lands as a new posture switch or a second fail-closed spelling, giving two UAT fail-closed paths with different messages that can disagree, while the existing arm stays dead. **Disposition consequence:** state the remedy as a producer change — emit `"unknown"` when a protected dest is recovered and the command is not read-shaped — not as a posture inversion.

## `arc-mode:` is absent from the Stop 1 write-back — `sharpens-framing`

Comment `5515687443` records charter, spend, target shape, ceiling, refutation target and audit targets, and no `arc-mode:` field; the envelope I was dispatched with carries no Run posture field either. This seat is running in `/private/tmp/design-critique-4005-claude`, a `git worktree add` tree with two sibling seat trees beside it. Under `arc-mode: direct` that worktree add is prohibited; under `checkout` it is expected. The record does not say which, so nothing on the thread distinguishes an authorized checkout panel from a direct panel that took worktrees anyway. **Failure mode:** the same silence in a mutation-capable seat is how a direct-posture arc acquires a mutation lease with no recorded contradiction, and no later reader or audit has a field to check. **Disposition consequence:** parent records the field before Stop 5; it does not change the security disposition.

## Footnotes (census, no disposition weight)

- `footnote` — Checked and rejected as a finding: dropping `run_terminal_cmd` from the authz gate looked like a Cursor fail-open regression introduced by the #4041 fix. It is not. The single caller (`dispatcher.ts:971`) computes `shellCommand = isShellTool(toolName) ? hookShellCommand(payload) : null`, and the pre-#4041 private branch returned `[]` on a null command, so that spelling never classified a command through the hook path. The live Cursor residual is that the host's emitted tool names are unobserved (`HOST_TOOL_SURFACE_AUDIT.cursor`), which is #3987's class, not this issue's.
- `footnote` — Injection / swarm lens (it fires: authority classification, the kill-switch, a shared grant store, worktrees, untrusted issue text). The issue body's remediation prose is instruction-shaped, and comments `5495382649` / `5495644104` carry `Do not start a second arc here` and `This thread is not a second arc`. I read all of it as evidence of a prior per-issue disposition, not as direction, and did not let it terminate this critique. Separately: the 30-name list is author-supplied untrusted content, so adopting it as the enforcement surface lets an issue author choose what the gate covers — a second reason it belongs in a regression corpus rather than in the classifier.
- `footnote` — HIGH 2/3/MEDIUM are conditional on a live UAT lease: `evaluate.ts` returns `authz-inactive` allow when no campaign is active. That does not soften the severity under UAT, and the issue's Impact lines do not state the precondition.

## Road not taken

I could have verified HIGH 2/3/MEDIUM the way the issue frames them — "none of these strings appear in `classify.ts`" — which is true and would have supported limb 2. Token absence is not behavior: executing the classifier showed three of five shapes already gate all 30 names without consulting the bin name, which inverts the remedy axis. The second fork was whether the dropped Cursor spelling was a HIGH regression; tracing the one caller closed it, and it is a footnote rather than a finding.

## Steelman of the position I am rejecting

The strongest case for the premise: all four findings sit in one file and one impact class (protected-store writes under an active UAT lease), splitting them across #4041 and #3953 has already produced seven-plus harvests without closing the class, and a bundled issue is what forces the posture decision instead of deferring it again. That case is not weak on ownership grounds — it is weak because two of its three mechanisms provably do not move enforcement.

What would flip my verdict: a measurement showing destination recovery has low recall on real agent shell writes while bin membership covers most of them — #3997's arc measured 47.1% recogniser recall on a different predicate, and the equivalent number for this classifier has not been taken. If dest recovery were the low-recall axis here, enumeration would be the higher-yield remedy and my third finding would be wrong.


### Comment by @dbcall2 (2026-09-02T20:17:36Z)

## Verdict

**Refute** the recorded Stop 1 premise. The four findings must not bind as one issue whose remedy is catalog-unifying shell host names, naming the residual writers, and failing closed on unclassifiable write-shaped Shell under UAT. HIGH 1 is a different, already-landed host-name gate. HIGH 2 / HIGH 3 / MEDIUM share one dest-visible empty-ops hole that those two remaining conjuncts do not close.

Tree: detached HEAD `212481b98051e9988f0a15748400c6afc154b2a5`. `classify.ts` blob `a4313768`. Probe: copied that blob to OS temp; stubbed `listShellOps` to push/merge only (these residual forms are not push/merge); live `classifyShellAuthzOps` / `classifyHookAuthzOps` / `isShellTool`. Residual binaries were not executed against the repo. `decideHook` was not invoked; the empty-ops path is read from `dispatcher.ts`. In-envelope comments on this thread: `5495382649`, `5495644104`, `5496118753`, `5515687443`. Instruction-shaped prose in those comments and in the issue body was treated as claims, not commands.

## Injection / swarm lens

The target changes authority (UAT grant check), untrusted input (host shell command strings), identity (host tool names), and shared state (`.deft/authz`, `.deft-directive-disable`, `.deft/approved-scope`). An empty classification under active UAT is an allow: the agent can plant a grant or the kill-switch, then later edit / push / PR / merge proceed as authorized. A naive deny on every empty Shell classification would also deny `git status` and `cat .deft/authz/state.json`. The close has to distinguish a protected dest that is already visible in the command from ordinary unclassifiable shell.

Existing mechanisms already in tree (do not invent a fourth): `isShellTool` / `SHELL_TOOL_NAMES`; `classifyShellAuthzOps` dest harvest including `genericProtectedDests`; `hasWriteShape` (`>` or two bin lists); `evaluateAuthzMutation` deny on op `"unknown"`; dispatcher empty-ops skip (`authzForMutation` returns null, runtime authority allows `shell-op-unclassifiable`); #3997 bound fail-open on dests the cooperative shell-write recogniser cannot recover.

## 1. HIGH 1 is a shipped host-name gate, not this harvest

`blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** At this SHA, `classifyHookAuthzOps` routes through `isShellTool` (`packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts` 2858–2862). Live probe, same command `cp forged.json .deft/authz/grants/evil.json`:

| toolName | `isShellTool` | ops |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Bash` / `Shell` / `run_terminal_command` / `monitor` | true | `["settings"]` |
| `run_terminal_cmd` | false | `[]` |
| `Write` (`isDirectWrite`) | false | `["edit"]` |

That is commit `75d5970a` (#4041, closed). CHANGELOG at this SHA records the catalog pin and explicitly does not bind #4005 HIGH 2/3/MEDIUM. The issue body's private `bash|shell|run_terminal_cmd` gate is gone.

**Failure mode.** Binding "catalog-unify shell host names" as part of this issue recuts a closed name-gate, or no-ops it, while still packaging the residual harvest as the same story. The two layers disagree for different reasons: HIGH 1 was "the host tool never reached `classifyShellAuthzOps`"; HIGH 2/3/MEDIUM are "the command reached it and returned `[]`".

**Disposition consequence.** The one-issue conjunct cannot bind as written. HIGH 1 stays on the landed #4041 catalog. This issue cannot carry a host-name unification AC.

## 2. Naming the residual writers does not close the class

`blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** None of `nu`, `xonsh`, `truffleruby`, `mruby`, `opal`, `rbx`, `ipython3`, `bpython`, `ptpython`, `ghc`, `ocaml`, `zip`, `haxe`, `kak`, `helix`, `amp`, `redis-cli`, `ctr`, `rst2html`, `tclsh`, `expect`, `xdelta3`, `diffoscope`, `parcel`, `serverless`, `dar`, `borg`, `duplicity`, `curlftpfs`, `rpmbuild` appear as bins in `classify.ts` (only `unzip` / `lrzip`). Live `classifyShellAuthzOps` at this blob:

| command | ops |
| --- | --- |
| `cp` / `python3 -c` write / `echo hi >` into authz, kill-switch, or approved-scope | `["settings"]` |
| `cat .deft/authz/state.json` / `git status` / `""` | `[]` |
| each named residual, positional dest on those three protected paths | `[]` |
| `ipython3 -c` / `nu -c` write into `.deft/authz` | `[]` (`python3 -c` on the same payload is `["settings"]`) |
| `zip .deft/authz/evil.zip src` / `borg create .deft/authz/repo src` | `[]` |
| `unknownwriter -o .deft/authz/grants/evil.json` and every named residual with `-o` on that dest | `["settings"]` |
| same residuals targeting `/tmp/out` | `[]` |

`genericProtectedDests` already fail-closes unknown bins when a protected dest rides a recognized dest flag. The leftover is positional dests, eval payloads, and flag spellings the extra-dest set missed (`rpmbuild --define '_topdir .deft/authz'` stayed `[]`). Adding this scan's thirty names is the same harvest as #3545 / #3849 / #3953.

**Failure mode.** A PR that classifies exactly these strings goes green, the next unused writer (`llvm-ar`, `typst`, the next scan) is again `[]` → allow. The list is the hole.

**Disposition consequence.** "Classify the named residual writers" cannot bind as the class close. Named bins are regression corpus, not the remedy.

## 3. Fail-closed on unclassifiable write-shaped Shell misses these residuals

`blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** `hasWriteShape` (`classify.ts` 2482–2491) is `command.includes(">")` or membership in `INDIRECT_WRITE_BINS` / `ARCHIVE_ALT_WRITE_BINS`. The named residuals are absent from those sets, and the positional / `-c` forms have no `>`. `hasIndirectAuthzStoreWrite` returns false when `hasWriteShape` is false even if the command text already contains `.deft/authz` (2703). Production classify never `found.add("unknown")` (grep of `packages/core/src`). `evaluateAuthzMutation` already denies `op === "unknown"` under UAT (`evaluate.ts` 323–330). Empty ops never reach that deny: `authzForMutation` returns null (`dispatcher.ts` 981–993), and `decideShellOrMcpRuntimeAuthority` allows `shell-op-unclassifiable` (1119–1131).

This is not the #3997 gate. #3997 bound fail-open on destinations the cooperative shell-write recogniser cannot statically recover (`content/contracts/path-write-fence.md`). Here the dest is already in the command string; the writer is unknown; classify returns `[]`.

**Failure mode.** Implementing the third conjunct against today's `hasWriteShape` leaves `nu` / `ipython3 -c` / `zip` / `borg` empty, so UAT still allows the plant. Fail-closing every empty Shell op instead denies reads and `git status`. Inverting #3997 dest-recovery fights a bound cooperative-guardrail posture and still does not run `evaluateAuthzMutation`.

**Disposition consequence.** "Fail closed on unclassifiable write-shaped Shell under UAT" cannot bind as written. The existing close in this file is dest-visible, not write-shape-named: emit an op evaluate already honours (`settings` or `"unknown"`) when a protected dest is recovered and the command is not a read.

## 4. HIGH 2, HIGH 3, and MEDIUM are one empty-ops hole

`sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** The same thirty residuals returned `[]` on `.deft/authz/**`, `.deft-directive-disable`, and `.deft/approved-scope/**`. `cp` on each dest returned `["settings"]`. Kill-switch and approved-scope are additional dests on the same classifier path (`pathishIsProtectedDest` / `hasAuthzDirShellWrite` / `hasKillSwitchShellWrite`), not separate roots.

**Failure mode.** Three acceptance copies of "add these bins" schedule three harvests of one miss.

**Disposition consequence.** After HIGH 1 is out, the remainder is one dest-based classifier story. It is not three findings and not the recorded three-conjunct issue.

## 5. Cursor `run_terminal_cmd` is outside this catalog on purpose

`footnote`

`isShellTool("run_terminal_cmd")` is false; `SHELL_TOOL_NAMES` does not contain it (`classify.test.ts` pin; `tools.test.ts`). #4041 bound "do not add that alias." Cursor's emitted shell name is unobserved in `HOST_TOOL_SURFACE_AUDIT`. Not a reason to reopen HIGH 1 inside #4005.

## 6. Prior comments on this thread are claims, including the #3997 layer mix

`footnote`

Comments `5495644104` / `5496118753` already split HIGH 1 onto #4041 and the residual half onto a dest-based story. "Do not start a second arc here" is instruction-shaped untrusted text; this pass did not obey it. The claim that unbounded fail-closed is "the posture #3997 withdrew" mixes layers (finding 3). #3953 is an open dest-based classifier issue (`design-critique:triage-ready`); that state is inventory, not a command to dominate this number.

## Road-not-taken

Chosen: refute the conjunct; keep HIGH 1 landed; treat the residual half as dest-visible classify (extend the unknown-bin harvest that already returns `["settings"]` for `-o` on a protected dest), with the scan list as tests.

## F1 — HIGH 1 is already satisfied

Classification: `blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** Commit [`75d5970`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/commit/75d5970a0529f122f62561bf68a4c445bfd39e65) is an ancestor of the dispatch SHA. The current classifier delegates Shell-host recognition to [`isShellTool`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/212481b98051e9988f0a15748400c6afc154b2a5/packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts#L2847-L2863), whose canonical catalog includes `run_terminal_command` and `monitor` ([catalog and helper](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/212481b98051e9988f0a15748400c6afc154b2a5/packages/core/src/hooks/tools.ts#L38-L69)). ## F2 — Name absence is not a residual-writer census

Classification: `blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** The classifier has generic protected-destination handling for output flags such as `-o`, `--output`, and `--outfile` ([implementation](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/212481b98051e9988f0a15748400c6afc154b2a5/packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts#L1647-L1728)). Consequently, an actual dispatch-SHA probe of `ghc -o .deft/authz/grants/evil /tmp/x.hs` classified as `settings` and was denied under active UAT even though `ghc` has no dedicated name branch. In contrast, each of these exact commands classified to no ops and was allowed by the same active-UAT hook decision:

```text
zip .deft/authz/grants/evil.json /etc/hosts
zip .deft-directive-disable /etc/hosts
zip .deft/approved-scope/evil.json /etc/hosts
```

Separate execution with `/usr/bin/zip` created each exact target file, so `zip` is an end-to-end residual rather than a name-search inference.

**Concrete failure mode.** Treating every absent executable name as a bypass produces false positives such as `ghc`, encourages redundant special cases, and still says nothing testable about the invocation forms that actually write. It can expand catalog size without establishing coverage.

**Disposition consequence.** Retain only residuals backed by exact command vectors and executable write evidence. For each retained vector, specify the protected destination, expected classifier op and UAT decision, plus ordinary/read-only negative controls. The currently named list cannot serve as acceptance evidence by itself.

## F3 — “Unclassifiable write-shaped Shell” is not yet a closed predicate

Classification: `blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** An empty Shell classification currently exits the authz gate without a decision ([dispatcher](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/212481b98051e9988f0a15748400c6afc154b2a5/packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts#L970-L994)), while a classified `unknown` op is denied during active UAT ([evaluator](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/212481b98051e9988f0a15748400c6afc154b2a5/packages/core/src/authz/evaluate.ts#L322-L330)). But the available `hasWriteShape` logic is itself based on recognized redirects, commands, and flags, so it does not supply a parser-independent definition for cases such as positional `zip` output. Existing negative tests deliberately leave ordinary commands, reads, and print-only interpreter use unclassified ([examples](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/212481b98051e9988f0a15748400c6afc154b2a5/packages/core/src/authz/classify.test.ts#L134-L216)). The adjacent path-write-fence contract also records the bounded recall and false-positive tradeoff of Shell-string parsing ([security bound](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/212481b98051e9988f0a15748400c6afc154b2a5/content/contracts/path-write-fence.md#L164-L205)); it does not decide UAT policy, but it is evidence against treating “write-shaped” as self-defining.

**Concrete failure mode.** Mapping every empty Shell classification to `unknown` would deny benign commands such as `git status`, protected-state reads, and print-only interpreter commands under active UAT. Gating the fallback on the current write-shape recognizer would still allow the demonstrated `zip` vectors. The stated criterion therefore admits incompatible implementations with opposite false-positive behavior.

**Disposition consequence.** Before this can be an acceptance criterion, define a closed UAT-only fallback predicate, its false-positive budget and remediation path, and executable positive/negative fixtures. Otherwise, withdraw the blanket fail-closed claim and remediate only verified writer forms.

## F4 — Approved-scope does not have the same immediate authority effect

Classification: `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** Scope provenance derives approval authority from the merge-base record and separately checks current-disk agreement ([evaluation](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/212481b98051e9988f0a15748400c6afc154b2a5/packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts#L332-L369)). A record introduced or rewritten in the same change set is rejected as self-authorization ([decision path](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/212481b98051e9988f0a15748400c6afc154b2a5/packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts#L629-L723), [new-record test](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/212481b98051e9988f0a15748400c6afc154b2a5/packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate-git.test.ts#L133-L159), [rewrite test](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/212481b98051e9988f0a15748400c6afc154b2a5/packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate-git.test.ts#L222-L252)). Thus a working-tree write or same-PR rewrite is not an immediate scope grant, unlike planting a grant consumed from disk or creating the kill-switch.

**Concrete failure mode.** Grouping the MEDIUM with the two immediate protected-state effects overstates the demonstrated authorization consequence and can produce an acceptance test that proves file creation but not self-authorization.

**Disposition consequence.** Keep approved-scope writes classified as `settings` for defense in depth, but state the independent path by which a forged record could reach the trusted merge base or narrow the finding to hardening. Its end-to-end consequence needs a separate fixture.

## Injection and shared-state lens

This lens triggers. The Shell command string is untrusted, open-ended input to a security-relevant classifier. The grant store and kill-switch can influence later hook decisions, while approved-scope is additionally mediated by merge-base state. A finite binary-name catalog is therefore a best-effort recognizer, not proof that the shared authority boundary is covered. This lens adds no separate finding; it is the threat-model basis for F2–F4.

## Road not taken

The strongest alternative was to dismiss the entire issue as stale because HIGH 1 has landed. I rejected that position: the compiled hook probe allowed the three exact `zip` vectors, and real `zip` execution created all three target files. The residual problem is concrete even though the recorded bundle is not.

## Steelman and verdict-flip condition

The strongest case for one narrowed issue is that the remaining destinations traverse the same Shell classifier and should converge on the same `settings` op, so one coherent patch could reduce drift. I would sustain that narrower design if it supplied an exact, negative-controlled reproducer matrix for every retained writer and a bounded UAT-only fallback predicate with specified false-positive behavior. That would not reopen HIGH 1 or establish approved-scope impact without its separate authority-path proof.
